ratios.label: Market value
ratios.meaning: What the whole company is worth on the stock market today.

ratios.formula: price ÷ earnings per share, last 12 months
ratios.label: Price to earnings (P/E)
ratios.meaning: How many years of the last year's profit you pay for. Lower is cheaper, but a low P/E can mean a business in trouble.
ratios.note: needs four consecutive quarters of earnings per share

ratios.label: Price to book (P/B)
ratios.meaning: Price against what the company's owners' money (assets less debts) is worth on the books.

ratios.label: Price to sales
ratios.meaning: Price against sales, useful when profits are small or negative.
ratios.note: needs four consecutive quarters

ratios.formula: (market value + debt − cash) ÷ operating profit, last 12 months
ratios.label: EV to operating profit
ratios.meaning: What a buyer would pay for the whole business, debt included, against its operating profit.
ratios.note: needs a balance sheet and positive operating profit

ratios.label: Earnings yield
ratios.meaning: Profit per ₹100 you pay for the share. The opposite of P/E.
ratios.note: needs four consecutive quarters of earnings per share

ratios.label: Dividend yield
ratios.meaning: Cash dividend per ₹100 you pay, over the last 12 months.
ratios.note: no dividend data

ratios.formula: profit to owners, last 12 months ÷ owners' equity
ratios.label: Return on equity (ROE)
ratios.meaning: Profit made on the owners' money in the business. Higher is better.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.label: Return on assets (ROA)
ratios.meaning: Profit made from everything the company owns.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.formula: (profit before tax + interest) ÷ (total assets − current liabilities)
ratios.label: Return on capital employed (ROCE)
ratios.meaning: Operating return on the money tied up in the business, before interest and tax.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.label: Operating margin
ratios.meaning: Operating profit kept from every ₹100 of sales, before interest, depreciation and tax. Compare within the same industry.
ratios.note: needs four consecutive quarters

ratios.label: Net profit margin
ratios.meaning: Profit kept from every ₹100 of sales after all costs and tax.
ratios.note: needs four consecutive quarters

ratios.formula: latest quarter ÷ same quarter a year earlier − 1
ratios.label: Sales growth (quarter, YoY)
ratios.meaning: How much sales grew against the same quarter last year.
ratios.note: not enough history to compare

ratios.formula: latest quarter ÷ same quarter a year earlier − 1
ratios.label: Profit growth (quarter, YoY)
ratios.meaning: How much profit grew against the same quarter last year.
ratios.note: not enough history to compare

ratios.formula: latest quarter ÷ same quarter a year earlier − 1
ratios.label: EPS growth (quarter, YoY)
ratios.meaning: Growth in profit for each share.
ratios.note: not enough history to compare

ratios.label: Sales growth (12 months)
ratios.meaning: Sales of the last 12 months against the 12 months before: smooths out a single odd quarter.
ratios.note: not enough history to compare

ratios.label: Profit growth (12 months)
ratios.meaning: Profit of the last 12 months against the 12 months before.
ratios.note: not enough history to compare

ratios.label: Debt to equity
ratios.meaning: Rupees borrowed for every ₹1 of owners' money. Lower is safer.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.formula: (borrowings − cash and investments) ÷ operating profit, last 12 months
ratios.label: Net debt to operating profit
ratios.meaning: Years of operating profit needed to repay debt after using cash. Lower is safer; negative means more cash than debt.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.formula: (profit before tax + interest) ÷ interest, last 12 months
ratios.label: Interest cover
ratios.meaning: How many times profit before interest and tax covers the interest bill. Below 2 is thin.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.label: Current ratio
ratios.meaning: Short-term assets against bills due within a year. Above 1.5 is comfortable.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.label: Quick ratio
ratios.meaning: Like the current ratio, but without stock that may be hard to sell fast.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.label: Asset turnover
ratios.meaning: Sales produced for every ₹1 of assets. Compare within the same industry.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.label: Days of sales owed by customers
ratios.meaning: How long customers take to pay. Lower and steady is better.
ratios.note: a figure it needs is not in the filing

ratios.formula: cash from operations ÷ net profit, year to date
ratios.label: Cash from operations vs profit
ratios.meaning: Whether profit is turning into cash. Near or above 1 is healthy.
ratios.note: profit is zero or a loss

ratios.formula: cash from operations − spending on plant, equipment and intangibles
ratios.label: Free cash flow (year so far)
ratios.meaning: Cash left after running the business and buying equipment.

ratios.formula: free cash flow ÷ sales, year to date
ratios.label: Free cash flow margin
ratios.meaning: Free cash flow per ₹100 of sales.
ratios.note: sales for the year so far not reported
